newsitem.title: JAPAN: No plan to change currency settlement -- Toyota.
newsitem.headline: No plan to change currency settlement -- Toyota.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Friday it has no plan to change the way it settles currency transactions even after Japanese firms are allowed to make exchange transactions without going through banks.

Asked if Toyota plans to make currency settlements between group firms after a revision of Japan's foreign exchange law takes effect next spring, Toyota executive vice president Akira Yokoi told Reuters: "We don't have plans to change payment terms."

Some Japanese exporters, such as Matsushita Electric Industrial Co, plan to exchange foreign currency earned from exports with group firms that need to make non-yen payments in order to trim risks from currency swings.
Earlier this month, Nissan Motor Co president Yoshikazu Hanawa said the liberalisation of Japan's foreign exchange law would help the company cut costs in overseas transactions.

Referring to Japan's ultra-low interest rates, Toyota's Yokoi said: "Japan's interest rates are too low relative to the rest of the world. But if Japan raises its interest rates that will lead to a higher yen. I want the authorities to make a proper decision taking into account the international balance, while watching (market) conditions."
He said no decision had yet been made as to whether Toyota would buy back more shares than it has already announced.
Toyota said last month it would buy back up to 27 million shares.
Earlier this month it said it would buy back up to 600,000 more shares to introduce a stock option scheme for employees.
